title: Prove the unique pair of active feedback operators (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration: the autonomous row at the unchanged two-edge saved-bank interface forces **F1=Q and F2=C1 Q**, even when both feedback operators vary arbitrarily in the predecessor algebra.

```text
R = B + Q^-1 F2 Q^-1 (K + F1 L)
L0 + L2 = 0, K0 + K2 = C1 D1
R0 + R2 - B2 = Q^-1 F2 Q^-1 C1 D1  => F2 = C1 Q
R1 = Q^-1 C1 (F1-Q) D1 = 0          => F1 = Q
```

The pair itself belongs to unpaidmoon #6961. That package proves the one-edge obstructions and explicitly leaves the all-pairs classification unproved. The new result is simultaneous uniqueness. The proof works in every associative unital ring with Q,D1 units, C1²=1 and QD1=D1Q. It survives quotients preserving the stated interface equations, without a faithful representation or word-length bound.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit unpaidmoon #6961 for the saved-bank identities and attaining pair; Cinna Davis #5220 for the active schedule and algebra; Dugongue / David Ganz #4948, Dillon #4933, Chris R / Clear1nsight and their retained native, compiler and precision lineage.

Card `joint-query-controller`, priority revision 8, **changed scope** to a fixed-interface classification. Canonical base is `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; source documents are pinned as provenance. The selected #7000 frontier is unchanged. A larger two-edge operator search cannot supply a different solution to this row contract.

## Evidence

- **Before:** #6961 supplies one pair and one-edge obstructions; its proof explicitly excludes classification of every pair.
- **After:** PROOF.md eliminates F1 from a two-column sum and forces both operators. The new standalone verifier checks 97,090 operator pairs across 75 fixtures, with exactly one solution each, 78,658 literal scalar inputs, three semantic controls and six invalid-fixture rejections. Fixtures include all 72 binary unit triples satisfying the reduced hypotheses, two ternary triples and a Z/4 triple with zero divisors.

Local CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. Both warning-strict direct modes, both registered commands, metadata/source pins, AST compilation, whitespace checks, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export/input-coverage check and both read-only Git-free exported modes passed. Normal and optimized generated hash-bound receipts agree exactly. Each registered mathematical command takes under one second locally, below its 120-second timeout.

Exact commands from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/two-edge-feedback-rigidity/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/two-edge-feedback-rigidity/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-edge-feedback-rigidity
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-edge-feedback-rigidity --check-source-history
```

Expected markers: `PASS_TWO_EDGE_FEEDBACK_RIGIDITY`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

The all-ring claim rests on the written proof. The finite fixtures corroborate the reduced interface; they are not native realizations or a replay of a predecessor scientific result. The inherited saved-bank row equations, chronology, phases, helper and owned-buffer contracts remain premises. The original witness is not a new construction, and its separate costs are not recomputed here.

No complete caller, independent target credit, native or physical tariff, improved κ or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. New saved sources, changed insertion points, different decoders or target rows are outside scope. All five selected assumptions remain. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No selected cold replay, predecessor scientific verifier, native, Lean or Docker suite ran.

## Related open work

- #7077 prices the same known pair and studies its unchanged scalar suffix; this PR proves uniqueness and does not recompute that bill.
- #7089 changes the saved-bank source and adds an operator at the final query; that changed source is outside this fixed two-edge interface.
- #7033 excludes D-exponent-0 owner-indexed decoding for the published feed; it keeps the feedback operators fixed while this PR classifies them.
- #7052 extends that decoding obstruction by a D3-inverse term; it changes decoder coefficients rather than these feedback operators.
- #7056 imposes D1^4=I on a residual decoder word; this uniqueness proof already tolerates extra relations preserving the interface and units, but does not evaluate its residual.

No same-number comparison with those cost or residual results was made.

## Open next questions

- Change one chronological saved source, derive its four independent input columns and price the complete restored endpoint. Availability and physical costs remain blockers.
- Specify a consumer for the unique coupled row with its full ordinary and recursive invoice. Two jobs in one output bank are not independent target credit.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At head `1927d11aee9c32a76ccaf531d0b223c966d637e0`, [run 43012497455](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43012497455), [plan job 130495338611](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43012497455/job/130495338611), the `Onboarding helper tests` step ran 760 tests with exactly one failure and 24 skips. The exact failing test is `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`. Its AssertionError says that '`make frontier7000-verify`' was not found in the current CI verification section.

The failure is in unchanged repository files: at canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, `certificates/selected-result.json` specifies `make frontier7000-verify`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. The record, document and test have identical bytes at the base and this PR head. This PR changes only its six package files. The `replay` job was skipped because `plan` failed, so no hosted mathematical replay or package certification occurred.

I read the logs and verified the same sole test failure, missing command, 760-test total and 24 skips in [run 42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314) and [run 42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790), and in this account's #7204 [run 43012524632](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43012524632) and #7199 [run 43001851217](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43001851217). Their replay jobs were also skipped.

Local registered, direct and exported checks remain the evidence described above. No fix, retrigger commit or job rerun was made for this repository-level failure; the head is unchanged. The own-open-PR refresh after the CLAIM found no additional PR studying this two-edge saved-bank row beyond the related work listed above.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Only a new isolated research package is added.

**Blast Radius:** package. No shared implementation, frozen source, selected certificate or predecessor credit is changed.
